newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS raises outlook on Canadian Pacific.
newsitem.headline: CBRS raises outlook on Canadian Pacific.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service on Thursday said it raised its outlook on Canadian Pacific Ltd's debt ratings to positive from stable.
The change in outlook comes after CP, a Montreal-based conglomorate, said it would sell its stake in waste management firm Laidlaw Inc.

The debt rating agency said the upgrade reflects the success of CP's corporate strategy which has increased the financial flexibility of the firm while reducing the volatility of the mainstream businesses through general economic cycles.

CBRS maintained its ratings of A-1(Low) and A(Low) on CP's commercial paper program and long-term debt. The C$1.0 billion commercial paper program is rated in the prime quality category and its debentures and notes are rated in the good quality rating catagory.

The agency said CP's major presence in key sectors of the Canadian economy, favorable debt leverage and strong financial flexibility provide the credit underpinning for a strengthening financial profile and rating outlook.
CP is expected to take advantage of the improving economy and should generate strong cashflow over the intermediate term, CBRS said.
The agency added that prospects of a sustainable performance and strong credit measurements in 1997 are high, which if extended can lead to a positive rating adjustment form current levels.
